3.	On April 25, 1859, Ferdinand de Lesseps of the _Compagnie universelle du Y maritime de X_ struck the ground with a pickaxe to mark the beginning of a massive project. It took ten years, 1.5 million laborers, and the deaths of an estimated 120,000 workers to complete the X Y. While a later massive project with a higher per-capita fatality rate garners more notoriety for its human toll, X is still the deadliest documented construction project in human history, by far. The company systematically underplayed the human cost, by focusing in its propaganda photographs on European engineers and the most-advanced machinery of the day, rarely showing the million people who actually made it happen. After it opened in 1869, the X Y helped strengthen the grip that Britain and France had on their prized Asian colonies. By drastically reducing the cost of shipping raw materials from India to Britain and finished goods in the other direction, the X Y accelerated the already-underway devastation of the Indian Z industry that had manufactured the majority of the world’s Zs for many centuries. ID X (8 points), Y (5 points), and Z (7 points).
